98	## 6. Image Handling
99	
100	Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":
101	
102	| Status | Source | Handling |
103	|--------|--------|----------|
104	| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
105	| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
106	| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |
107	
108	**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
109

117

121	| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |

127	## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework
128	
129	### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document
130	
131	After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.
132	
133	**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.
134	
135	**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.
136	
137	**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):
138	
139	| Marker | Purpose |
140	|--------|---------|
141	| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
142	| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |
143

150	- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory

153	
154	Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.

157	
158	- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
159	- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
    <!-- 
    分组柱状图模板
    用途: 多系列数据对比
    适用场景: 多产品/时期/分类对比、同比环比分析
    支持: 4组 × 3系列（可调整为3-6组，2-4系列）
    与普通柱状图区别: 每个类别下有多个并排柱子，用于对比
    -->
    
    <defs>
        <!-- 系列1渐变（蓝色） -->
        <linearGradient id="groupGrad1" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="0%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#2196F3;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#1976D2;stop-opacity:1" />

        <!-- 系列2渐变（绿色） -->
        <linearGradient id="groupGrad2" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="0%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#4CAF50;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#388E3C;stop-opacity:1" />
        </linearGradient>
        
        <!-- 系列3渐变（橙色） -->
        <linearGradient id="groupGrad3" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="0%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#FF9800;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#F57C00;stop-opacity:1" />
        </linearGradient>
        
        <!-- 阴影 -->
        <filter id="groupShadow">
            <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="2"/>
            <feOffset dx="0" dy="1"/>
            <feComponentTransfer>
                <feFuncA type="linear" slope="0.25"/>
            </feComponentTransfer>
            <feMerge>

                <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>

    <!-- 背景 -->

    <!-- 标题 -->

          font-size="32" font-weight="bold" fill="#2C3E50">
        <tspan>各季度产品线销售对比</tspan>
    </text>
    
    <text x="60" y="105" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
          font-size="18" fill="#7F8C8D">
        <tspan>2025年度 · 单位：百万元</tspan>
    </text>
    
    <!-- 图例 -->

              font-size="15" fill="#5D6D7E">
            <tspan>产品线C</tspan>
        </text>
    </g>
    
    <!-- 图表区域 -->

        <line x1="140" y1="300" x2="1180" y2="300" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4,4"/>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="topGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <linearGradient id="mooreGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#3B82F6"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <linearGradient id="internetGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#8B5CF6"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <linearGradient id="mobileGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#D4AF37"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#F59E0B"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>

  <!-- White background for content page -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>

  <!-- Top gradient bar -->
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="6" fill="url(#topGradient)"/>

  <!-- Key message bar (gold left decoration) -->
  <rect x="40" y="30" width="4" height="50" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <rect x="44" y="30" width="1196" height="50" fill="#0D1117"/>
  <text x="60" y="62" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#D4AF37">
    <tspan>KEY INSIGHT</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="180" y="62" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF">
    <tspan>The spark: ChatGPT ignited a Cambrian explosion of AI innovation not seen since the early internet</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Page title -->
  <text x="40" y="130" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#111827">
    <tspan>Six Decades of Technological Progress</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="40" y="165" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" fill="#6B7280">
    <tspan>Converged to Enable Generative AI</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Three waves visualization -->
  <!-- Wave 1: Moore's Law -->
  <g transform="translate(80, 210)">
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="340" height="200" rx="8" fill="#1E40AF" opacity="0.1"/>
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="340" height="8" rx="4" fill="url(#mooreGrad)"/>
    <text x="20" y="50" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="48" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E40AF">
      <tspan>6</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="80" y="50" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#111827">
      <tspan>decades</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="20" y="90" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#111827">
      <tspan>Moore's Law</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="20" y="120" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">
      <tspan>Compute horsepower to process</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="20" y="140" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">
      <tspan>exaflops of data</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="20" y="170" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#9CA3AF">
      <tspan>1965 — 2023</tspan>
    </text>
  </g>

  <!-- Arrow 1 -->
  <polygon points="450,310 480,290 480,330" fill="#D4AF37"/>

  <!-- Wave 2: Internet -->
  <g transform="translate(520, 210)">
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="340" height="200" rx="8" fill="#7C3AED" opacity="0.1"/>
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="340" height="8" rx="4" fill="url(#internetGrad)"/>
    <text x="20" y="50" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="48" font-weight="bold" fill="#7C3AED">
      <tspan>4</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="80" y="50" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#111827">
      <tspan>decades</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="20" y="90" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#111827">
      <tspan>Internet</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="20" y="120" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">
      <tspan>Trillions of tokens of</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="20" y="140" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">
      <tspan>training data (accelerated by COVID)</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="20" y="170" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#9CA3AF">
      <tspan>1989 — 2023</tspan>
    </text>
  </g>

  <!-- Arrow 2 -->
  <polygon points="890,310 920,290 920,330" fill="#D4AF37"/>

  <!-- Wave 3: Mobile/Cloud -->
  <g transform="translate(960, 210)">
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="280" height="200" rx="8" fill="#F59E0B" opacity="0.1"/>
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="280" height="8" rx="4" fill="url(#mobileGrad)"/>
    <text x="20" y="50" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="48" font-weight="bold" fill="#D4AF37">
      <tspan>2</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="80" y="50" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="24" fill="#111827">
      <tspan>decades</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="20" y="90" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#111827">
      <tspan>Mobile + Cloud</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="20" y="120" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">
      <tspan>Supercomputer in every</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="20" y="140" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#6B7280">
      <tspan>human's palm</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="20" y="170" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#9CA3AF">
      <tspan>2000 — 2023</tspan>
    </text>
  </g>

  <!-- Convergence arrow -->
  <rect x="80" y="460" width="1120" height="3" fill="#D4AF37"/>

  <!-- Result box -->
  <rect x="80" y="490" width="1120" height="120" rx="8" fill="#0D1117"/>
  <text x="120" y="540" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">
    <tspan>The Convergence Result</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="120" y="575" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#9CA3AF">
    <tspan>Foundation models emerged as a new paradigm — enabling AI to generate text, images, code, and more at unprecedented scale</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <rect x="0" y="660" width="1280" height="60" fill="#F9FAFB"/>
  <text x="40" y="695" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">
    <tspan>Source: Sequoia Capital Analysis</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="1240" y="695" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#D4AF37" text-anchor="end">
    <tspan>2</tspan>
  </text>
</svg>

  </text>
  <text x="500" y="500" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#9CA3AF">

    <tspan>3</tspan>
  </text>
</svg>

# 01_cover

[Transition] Today, we're examining a pivotal shift in the generative AI landscape — what Sequoia Capital has termed "Act Two."

The spark came in late 2022: ChatGPT's launch ignited a Cambrian explosion of AI innovation not seen since the early internet. AI researchers became rockstars, hacker houses overflowed with autonomous agents, and the arXiv printing press worked overtime.

But excitement quickly turned to hysteria — and then to a quiet reckoning. Every company became an "AI copilot," inboxes filled with undifferentiated pitches, and whispers spread that generative AI wasn't actually useful.

That's the story we're unpacking today: the transition from Act One's technology-out approach to Act Two's customer-back model. And the data — especially the retention gap — tells the tale.

Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_decades_of_convergence

Generative AI's emergence is not a sudden event — it's the culmination of six decades of technological progress.

Six decades of Moore's Law gave us the compute horsepower to process exaflops of data. Four decades of the internet — accelerated dramatically by COVID — produced trillions of tokens of training data. And two decades of mobile and cloud computing put a supercomputer in every human's palm.

These three waves converged. The result: foundation models emerged as a new paradigm, enabling AI to generate text, images, code, and more at unprecedented scale.

ChatGPT was the spark that ignited commercial interest. But as we'll see, that interest hasn't automatically translated into sustainable products.

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_genai_outpaces_saas

Despite the skepticism, generative AI has had a more successful commercial start than SaaS ever did.

Startups crossed **$1 billion in revenue** in months — a milestone that took SaaS years to reach.

Look at the standouts: ChatGPT became the fastest-growing application in history, with strong product-market fit among students and developers. Midjourney hit hundreds of millions in revenue with just 11 employees. And Character.ai users spend an average of 2 hours per session — extraordinary engagement.

[Pause]

But here's the critical nuance: these successes don't change the reality that many AI companies lack product-market fit or sustainable competitive advantage. The revenue is real, but the retention story is mixed.

Which brings us to the data on slide four.

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 04_retention_gap

This is the most important slide in the deck.

Mobile app retention data reveals a stark gap between established consumer apps and AI-first companies. Look at the incumbents: WhatsApp at 85%, Instagram and YouTube both at 64%, TikTok at 60%. Even the lower performers like Candy Crush and Duolingo hold above 30%. The **median for incumbents is 51%**.

Now look at AI-first companies: Character.ai leads at 41%, then Runway at 27%, then Remini, ChatGPT, and Lensa all clustered at 12-14%. The **median for AI-first is just 14%**.

[Pause]

That's a 3.6x retention gap. For every user an incumbent retains, an AI-first app is losing nearly four out of five.

This is why the $1B revenue milestone, while impressive, doesn't tell the whole story. Without retention, revenue is fragile. And without stickiness, the "winner" in AI might just be the first mover who captured lightning in a bottle — but can't hold it.

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 05_incumbent_monthly_usage

The incumbent benchmark sets an even higher bar when we look at monthly active usage.

YouTube leads at 85% MAU. Instagram at 73%, TikTok at 69%, Snapchat at 67%. Even the "lower" apps like Candy Crush still hit 48%. The median across all incumbents is **63%**.

Think about what that means for AI-first companies trying to compete. They're not just fighting for attention — they're fighting for habit formation against apps that have years of behavioral conditioning behind them.

The 63% MAU median isn't just a number; it's proof that consumers have deeply embedded these apps into their daily routines. Breaking that habit requires more than a good AI model — it requires solving a real human problem in a way that's stickier than the incumbent.

Duration: 1.5 minutes

---

# 06_act1_vs_act2

So what's the path forward? Sequoia frames the market as transitioning between two acts.

**Act 1 was Technology-Out** — foundation models as the entire solution. Think novelty demos that impressed but didn't stick. Lightweight wrappers with no defensible moat. Companies that used AI as the hammer and looked for nails.

**Act 2 is Customer-Back** — foundation models as a piece of a comprehensive solution. New editing interfaces that make workflows stickier. Multi-modal workflows that handle complex end-to-end tasks. Companies that start with the human problem and work backward to technology.

[Pause]

Act 2 exemplars prove this works. **Harvey** builds custom LLMs for elite law firms — solving a high-stakes, complex workflow end-to-end. **Glean** crawls and indexes workspaces for relevant enterprise AI — embedded in how people actually work. **Character** and **Ava** are building digital companions — which explains Character's outlier 41% retention rate.

The pattern: companies that build comprehensive solutions around human needs, using AI as one ingredient among many, are the ones pulling ahead.

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 07_market_map_evolution

This transition is so significant that even how we categorize the market is changing.

Act 1 organized by model modality — text models, image models, code models. A taxonomy built around technology capabilities.

Act 2 organizes by use case — legal, enterprise search, companionship, creative tools. A taxonomy built around human needs.

[Transition] The shift reflects the maturation of the market. Applications are now built around what people need to accomplish, not what technical capabilities are available.

And notice the increasingly multi-modal nature of Act 2 solutions. Legal work isn't just text — it involves document review, contract analysis, and communication. Enterprise search spans emails, files, chats, and databases. The best AI products solve end-to-end workflows, not narrow tasks.

This reorganization mirrors the broader Act 1 to Act 2 transition — from technology hammer to actual value delivery.

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 08_key_takeaways

Let's close with five actionable implications.

**One: Retention is the critical challenge.** AI-first apps at 14% median vs. 51% for incumbents — a 3.6x gap. Revenue without retention is fragile.

**Two: Foundation models are infrastructure, not product.** Act 2 companies build comprehensive solutions with AI as one component — not the entire offering.

**Three: Multi-modal, workflow-integrated solutions win.** Stickiness comes from embedding in how people actually work, not from standalone AI capabilities.

**Four: The $1B+ revenue milestone proves real demand exists.** Despite hype cycles and skepticism, commercial traction is undeniable.

**Five: Companies solving end-to-end human problems will define Act 2.** Character.ai's 41% retention approaching incumbent levels suggests companionship and entertainment may be generative AI's strongest consumer use case.

[Pause]

The retention gap is the signal. Act 2 companies that solve real human problems end-to-end — with stickiness built into workflows — are the ones positioned to win.

For investors: focus on companies with demonstrated retention and defensible workflows, not just impressive demos.

For founders: foundation models are infrastructure. Build comprehensive solutions around human needs.

Duration: 2 minutes

The 8-slide presentation has been successfully generated and saved to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`.

**Slide Summary:**
1. **Cover** - "Generative AI's Act Two: From Technology Hammer to Real Value" (Sequoia Capital, September 2023)
2. **Decades of Convergence** - Three waves: Moore's Law (6 decades), Internet (4 decades), Mobile/Cloud (2 decades)
3. **GenAI Outpaces SaaS** - >$1B revenue, ChatGPT fastest-growing, Midjourney 11 employees, Character.ai 2hr sessions
4. **Retention Gap** - Horizontal bar chart showing incumbents (51% median) vs AI-first (14% median), with 3.6x gap highlighted
5. **Incumbent Monthly Usage** - Vertical bar chart showing YouTube 85% down to Candy Crush 48% (63% median)
6. **Act 1 vs Act 2** - Two-column comparison with Harvey, Glean, Character, Ava as Act 2 exemplars
7. **Market Map Evolution** - Shift from modality-based to use-case-driven categorization
8. **Key Takeaways** - 5 actionable implications for investors and founders

All data comes directly from the source brief. The presentation uses an Exhibit-style dark/light theme with gold accents, professional data-forward styling suitable for Sequoia Capital attribution.
